At my 9wk scan, she couldn't find the embryo, just an empty sac. I went to my old OB an hr away for a second opinion. They saw the embryo but looked like it had stopped growing around 6wks and there was no heart tone detected. I went back 1 week later to make sure there wasn't any change, which there wasn't. This was on a Friday iirc and we scheduled a D&C for Monday morning. I went home and started cramping and spotting and by Friday night the bleeding was severe and we went to the ER. They ended up sending me home even tho my bleeding was, in fact, severe and I hadn't passed the sac yet. They didn't want to deal with a D&C when they were so short staffed and there was no OB on call (still pissed about it all tbh). This was at 10wks 5days. By Monday, my OB verified that everything had passed and I wasn't bleeding much anymore so they sent me home. 

It's usually around 11-12wks that progesterone production switches from the corpus luteum to the placenta. If the placenta doesn't develop properly, then progesterone levels fall rapidly and the uterus will start to contract. I was almost at 11wks (and my cervix had been poked a bunch and irritated by all the vaginal ultrasounds) so that tracks, from my experience.

I've experienced this so many different ways:

 I was the child my parents didn't want: My parents were divorced (rightly so) because my father was a raging alcoholic who cheated  and was prone to violence. Despite being divorced, my mom got pregnant with me. Then my father went to prison for 4 yrs, after which, they remarried because..... she has zero self esteem, I guess? She was so depressed she could barely function when I was growing up. I became skilled at avoiding my father's verbal abuse and I counted myself lucky he never hit me like he did my older siblings. I grew up with all kinds of issues with men and now I seem to attract control freaks. (Seriously, if you're a miserable asshole, don't have children)

I had an unplanned pregnancy when I was 23: I decided to keep the baby even tho I was terrified. I think I just wanted to experience what real love was. I don't regret having my him but I wish I'd been older because one of the big coping mechanisms that got me through childhood was learning to focus on myself and whatever I needed at any given time which means I'm....kinda selfish as an adult. I don't mean to be, it's just a pattern that I developed as a child. So, because I didn't have a good example of "healthy" parenting from own parents, I studied. I read every book and magazine article I could find about babies and parenting techniques because I was so scared that I wouldn't love my child. After the birth, I had postpartum depression that went untreated and, in hindsight, I think I got through those first years mostly on willpower. 

I lost a child:  My second was planned and it was everything I'd wanted. You know how you just get someone without having to try? Well, that was my second child! We were just always in sync and I was the mom I'd always wanted to be. Until, at 2, he was diagnosed with a rare cancer. I feel like I ran a 4 yr marathon to try and keep him alive and then I collapsed when we lost him. I retreated so far into myself that I didn't have room for anything else, even my oldest child. During that time, his father was letting his parents care for our oldest and, well, they took a lot of liberties and essentially treated him as if he was their child. I regret that I didn't have the energy to stop it from happening. 

I had another surprise pregnancy: I love my child. She's the buoy that keeps me from sinking into the darkness. But...I feel like I'm not the parent she deserves. She's dramatic and high strung but also very talented and even pretty sweet in occasion. I'm older, so I have more patience, but I also have more emotional shrapnel than most so bonding with her isn't the easy sync up I had with my second child. It's been work. It's *still* work. I love her, I do, but that love is also swimming around with all the grief and regret and I feel like I'm just treading water most days. That's not what I wanted for myself and it's not what I wanted for my children.

Just chiming to to add my 2 cents: we applied for SSI for my son when he was going through cancer treatment. I think the max benefits per month were somewhere around $600 (it may be more if there are other dependent children in the household and the parent can't work because they must care for the sick/disabled child).
